source.title: OrtSAE: Orthogonal Sparse Autoencoders Uncover Atomic Features
source.authors: Anton Korznikov; Andrey V. Galichin; Alexey Dontsov; Oleg Y. Rogov; Elena Tutubalina; I. Oseledets

page_placements.theme: Feature composition and cross-method granularity at a fixed dictionary size

record.tranche_reason: The study compares SAE training objectives and reports that orthogonality and Matryoshka training change or reduce measured absorption and composition. It does not sweep dictionary size.
record.gate_note: Relevant results include absorption and composition metrics, plus qualitative feature decompositions and cross-method feature uniqueness. Reconstruction and downstream-task scores are not rows because they do not measure splitting, absorption, or composition. The qualitative decomposition examples use the same stated dictionary size for the SAE variants.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs with different objectives (ReLU, BatchTopK, Matryoshka, orthogonality-penalised OrtSAE) at a fixed size of 65,536 latents on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B. It reports SAEBench absorption rates for each. Lower absorption under Matryoshka and OrtSAE bears on V6's claim that the objective shapes absorption. The nonzero absorption in standard SAEs bears on V4 in new models. Dictionary size is never varied, so V1, V2, V3 and V5 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that the orthogonality penalty in OrtSAE reduces absorption (by 65%) and composition (by 15%) compared with traditional SAEs, approaching Matryoshka. They report 9% more distinct features, lower clustering, +6% on spurious correlation removal, and on-par reconstruction and downstream performance.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a chunk-wise orthogonality penalty to SAE training and compares against ReLU, BatchTopK, and Matryoshka variants; dictionary size is held at 65536 in the described experiments rather than swept.
record.method_sensitivity: Composition and absorption metrics vary with SAE method; Appendix C also reports modest increases in these metrics as OrtSAE chunk count rises.

fits_no_version.finding: MetaSAE composition rate is lower for OrtSAE (0.340 and 0.316) and Matryoshka (0.349 and 0.323) than for BatchTopK (0.490 and 0.461). ReLU is mixed (0.527 and 0.413).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed dictionary size, SAE training objectives change how far latents are composites of other latent directions (feature composition).

fits_no_version.finding: At a 0.2 cosine threshold, 9% of OrtSAE features are unique, versus 1.5% of BatchTopK features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed dictionary size, changing the SAE training method can yield a different set of decoder features, including features classified as unique by a cosine threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected BatchTopK features (Queen, climate, jaw, module) are shown as sparse combinations of 2–3 OrtSAE features at the same size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed stated dictionary size, decoder features learned by one SAE method can be represented as combinations of features learned by another method.

record.problems: Only one dictionary size, m=65536, is reported, so the claim's size-scaling relationship is not tested. Absorption and composition are assessed using proxy metrics; uncertainty estimates are not reported, and some comparisons are presented only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported absorption or composition result was left out. Core performance and downstream benchmark metrics were excluded because they do not measure the claim's splitting or absorption/composition behavior.

untested.parts: No dictionary-size sweep; only m=65536 is used.
No size-related splitting is tested and no open SAE releases are used.
Nested, geometrically close families mirroring a concept hierarchy are not tested.
Whether changing dictionary size fixes absorption is not tested. Persistence across L0 is shown only in Fig 4b, without readable BatchTopK values.
No larger-vs-smaller dictionary comparison is made. The decompositions are cross-method at a fixed size.
Whether absorption says little about the model's own units is not tested. Correlated or hierarchical inputs are not manipulated.

missing.what: OrtSAE absorption and composition as a function of chunk count K in {4..64}: absorption rises from about 0.15 to 0.20 but stays below traditional SAEs
BatchTopK and ReLU absorption across L0 from 25 to 130, needed to judge whether changing sparsity removes absorption

record.verdict_notes: All SAEs use m=65536, so no size-scaling claim is tested. No uncertainty estimates are reported. In the layer-12 results, the per-L0 values are figure-only. The citation of Leask et al. is used only for its MetaSAE method, so this study is not an original-source replication.

versions.untested_parts: No increase in dictionary size is tested, and the study does not measure whether child features partition a smaller feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
The study uses multiple models and layers, but does not test the claimed size-related splitting pattern or report open SAE release results.
No nested, geometrically close feature families that mirror a concept hierarchy are tested.
The study measures absorption, but does not test the stated parent-versus-child firing holes as dictionary size changes, or whether changing size or sparsity fixes them.
The study compares SAE methods, not larger and smaller dictionaries; its same-size comparisons cannot test the stated size-related decomposition or completeness claim.

The study compares orthogonality, Matryoshka, and traditional SAE objectives on absorption and composition metrics. It does not establish that the measured effects say little about the model's own units.
